pl-l2d34c2-d1e108.summary: States that the first cause and origin of sin was a good thing, since before the first sin there was no evil to arise from; it arose first in the angel, then in man; the angel was a good nature of God; evil did not arise from God, nor from another than the angel; so it arose from good.

pl-l2d34c2-d1e111.summary: Cites Augustine's reply to Julian, who said that if sin is from nature, nature is evil: evil works come from evil will as bad fruit from a bad tree, but whence the evil will except from good? Angel and man were God's good works before evil will arose in them; so evil arises from good, and no evil preceded the evil will. Thus the first cause of evil was good nature, and it caused the evil will.
claims: No evil preceded the first evil will.
Good nature was the cause of evil will.

pl-l2d34c2.summary: Holds that the first cause and origin of sin was a good thing, since before the first sin there was no evil from which it could arise. Sin arose first in the angel, then in man, both good natures of God; it arose not from God nor from another but from the angel, hence from good. Augustine against Julian: all evil works come from evil will as fruit from an evil tree, but the evil will arose only from good, the angel or man, God's good works; so no evil preceded the evil will, which had its origin from good.
claims: The first origin of sin was a good thing.
Before the first sin there was no evil from which it could arise.
Sin arose first in the angel, then in man, both good natures.
Evil works come from evil will; evil will arose from good nature.
